note.question: How do bilateral ratings that reveal provider quality and customer service cost reshape application sorting, provider pricing, platform commission revenue, and competition relative to unilateral provider ratings?
note.overview: The paper solves a three-stage competitive-search and matching game. Providers strategically post prices, heterogeneous customers direct applications, capacity-constrained providers select applicants, and prices satisfy a pure-strategy Nash best-response system.

components.label: Symmetric pure-strategy Nash pricing equilibrium with directed-search application and acceptance subgames
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Symmetric pure-strategy Nash pricing equilibrium with directed-search application and acceptance subgames. Customer applications equalize expected utility across providers used with positive probability, taking congestion and acceptance into account. Provider prices satisfy p_j^*=argmax_{p_j^0} pi_j^0(p_j^0;p_H^*,p_L^*) in Equation (5). Proposition 2 establishes multiple price equilibria under the main bilateral-rating assumptions.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: First, all providers simultaneously post publicly observed prices. Second, all customers simultaneously submit at most one application, using mixed application strategies when indifferent. Third, each capacity-one provider receiving applications accepts the lowest-cost applicant. Service is delivered and the provider pays commission delta to the platform.
